claims: Finite engineering acceptance for the final version; not original gate equivalence, not a formal protocol proof, not a production-readiness claim.
supersedes: acceptance/v1.json (kept as a historical record with its receipts under artifacts/acceptance-v1/)
growth_rule: Each roadmap stage appends its own phase after its specification is approved. A phase may replace tests of an earlier phase only by updating v1_mapping so that every v1 property still names at least one final test that checks it no more weakly; scripts/test_verify_gate.py enforces that the mapping is complete and resolvable, and independent review judges strength.

13.title: S4: membership changes, one server at a time
13.notes: Since S4 tools/cluster.py creates every test cluster by bootstrapping node 1 and adding the others through membership requests, so every earlier integration test also exercises the add path. Tests whose only change is a constructor signature (Snapshot::new takes voters, AppendResponse carries last_log_index) are not listed in modified_tests.

14.title: S5: group commit, batched replication, deltas instead of whole states
14.notes: Since S5 Persist carries a Delta instead of a whole DurableState and the core proposes writes in batches (ProposeBatch); tests whose only change is reading delta fields instead of state fields are listed in modified_tests. tools/cluster.py writes history.json once at close (lesson 14), which changes no test's assertion.

limits: Original required-files, fingerprint and script semantics are unavailable.
Named test discovery and execution do not establish assertion quality; independent review required.
Subprocess tests cover process crashes, not arbitrary storage hardware power loss.
Format 1 data is neither read nor converted; it is reproducible only from git tag v1-baseline-verified-20261112.
Truncation at or inside a record, a missing file and replacement by an older complete file are outside per-record checksum detection.
The mutation report shows that each named test fails for one planted mistake; it does not show the tests are complete.
Snapshots are taken synchronously in the node's actor; their pause is traced but no availability bound is claimed.
The key-value data and the number of clients are not bounded; compaction stops when a snapshot would exceed 64 MiB.
ReadIndex reads are served by the leader only; there is no check-quorum, so an isolated leader's reads wait until they time out.
Read latency numbers in read-benchmark.json are recorded for comparison only and are not acceptance thresholds.
Mutation reports before 2026-11-13 (S1, S2 tags) were produced with one shared cargo target directory and may mix mutants; only reports with an isolation field are isolated.
Membership changes (S4) have no formal proof; the evidence is the dissertation, the 2015 raft-dev fix and finite tests, including a scripted replay of the 2015 counterexample.
Operator mistakes are not detected: bootstrapping twice, or re-adding an ID with a wiped data directory, can break safety (docs/MEMBERSHIP.md N2).

Catch-up is timed in heartbeats, not wall-clock time; a removed node keeps running until stopped, and re-adding a still-running removed node may make the leader step down once (MEMBERSHIP.md N5, N6, N8).
The simulator uses five node slots; configurations of six or seven nodes are exercised only by unit tests of the majority rule.

The independent review of S1-S4 (docs/INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_S1_S4.md) was done by a different model than the one that implemented S2-S4, but by the same model that drafted the S1 specification and its first commit; for S1 it is independent by session only.

The simulator's administrator sends one membership request at a time and its clients stop after 64 operations per seed; two concurrent changes, and reads late in a run, are covered by unit tests only (left for S6).
S5 performance numbers in write-benchmark.json are recorded for comparison only; acceptance gates on counts (barriers per queued batch, entries copied per write), measured in unit tests.
Group commit batches only writes already queued when the actor looks; there is no delay to collect larger batches, and no pipelining or parallel leader write (docs/PERFORMANCE.md D1, D2).

reserved_header_fields_must_be_pristine.note: S1 required the WAL start fields to hold fixed values. S2 uses them for the snapshot position, so the replacement checks their relations instead: seven inconsistent combinations are each refused with the file unchanged, a consistent non-default start is accepted, and a base without its snapshot file is refused.

quorum_is_two_of_three.note: V1 checked has_quorum over the fixed nodes 1/2/3: no quorum for none, one or a duplicated node, quorum for any two, node 4 invalid. S4 removes the fixed set. The replacements check the majority for every configuration size 1..=7 at the exact boundary (just enough passes, one short fails), that members outside the configuration never count, that a set cannot count a node twice, that a missing configuration has no quorum, and that node IDs 0 and 8 are refused while 1..=7 are accepted.

tests/integration/test_snapshot.py::test.note: S2 asserted a new GET raised effect_count by one. S3 D3 removes GETs from the state machine, so it now asserts effect_count is unchanged and additionally that the GET left the leader's durable_sequence unchanged

tests/history/test_checker.py::test_unse.note: showed the rejection with a GET; GETs no longer pass the session table, so it uses a Put and adds a read

saturated_outbound_pool_does_not_starve_.note: sent a GET to make the leader replicate into a saturated pool; since S3 a GET waits for ReadIndex and sends nothing, so the test stopped exercising the pool and the mutant survived. It now sends a Put; the control passes and the mutant is detected (lesson 07) S4 (13): Its hand-made leader now holds a three-node configuration entry: since S4 a leader replicates only to the voters of its configuration, and without one the Put would send nothing and the pool would not be exercised (the lesson 07 failure again). 2026-11-14: its hand-made actor names the three fields that replaced snapshot_too_large (lesson 13); nothing else changed. S5 (14): Its WAL now first saves the core's starting state: since S5 the node persists deltas, which must connect to what is on disk. 2026-11-15 (independent review S5, F6): since S5 the actor answers a status that arrives together with a write before it proposes that write, so with the planted mistake the one-second status check still passed and the test then waited for ever for the actor to stop (the S4 code failed it in 2.1 s). It now asks for a second status after the write was proposed (batched_writes must be 1) and bounds the wait for Stop; the mutant fails it in about one second. The assertion it had is kept; two are added.

single_leader_per_term.note: A node without a configuration no longer campaigns (S4), so the test starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1, term 1 instead of an empty log; every term and index it asserts moved up by one, the asserted behaviour is the same.

vote_persist_intent_before_reply.note: A node without a configuration no longer campaigns (S4), so the test starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1, term 1 instead of an empty log; every term and index it asserts moved up by one, the asserted behaviour is the same. The follower half still starts empty: an unconfigured node may vote. S5 (14): Persist carries a Delta since S5; the test reads term and vote from it instead of from a whole state. Same assertions.

previous_term_entry_requires_current_ter.note: The first entry is now a configuration entry (a leader counts only voters of its configuration), indexes unchanged. The RAM-only sub-check now has entry 1 durable and entry 2 only in the leader's RAM, both held by follower 2: it asserts commit 1, not 2, where it used to assert commit 0 for an empty durable log, so it still shows that a RAM-only self match does not count.

conflicting_suffix_repaired.note: Asserted that the durability barrier is the first effect. Since lesson 09 the Applies of entries committed before the barrier come first (a barrier's completion may commit and apply more), so it now asserts that the barrier precedes the AppendResponse and that nothing is applied after the barrier.

append_response_cannot_inflate_match_ind.note: A node without a configuration no longer campaigns (S4), so the test starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1, term 1 instead of an empty log; every term and index it asserts moved up by one, the asserted behaviour is the same.

replicated_get_linearizable.note: A node without a configuration no longer campaigns (S4), so the test starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1, term 1 instead of an empty log; every term and index it asserts moved up by one, the asserted behaviour is the same.

read_waits_for_a_committed_entry_of_its_.note: Its leader fixture starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1 (S4: no configuration, no election); readIndex values and indexes moved up by one.

replies_to_requests_sent_before_the_read.note: Its leader fixture starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1 (S4: no configuration, no election); readIndex values and indexes moved up by one.

reads_never_write_durable_state.note: Its leader fixture starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1 (S4: no configuration, no election); readIndex values and indexes moved up by one.

reads_fail_when_leadership_is_lost.note: Used a higher-term RequestVote to depose the leader; since S4 a leader ignores a higher-term RequestVote (docs/MEMBERSHIP.md section 9.4), so the higher term now arrives in an AppendEntries from that term's leader, and the test also asserts the new term. compaction_only_covers_applied_entries.note: Index 1 is now a configuration entry: a snapshot records the configuration at its position, so a log without one cannot be compacted. It additionally asserts the snapshot's voters.

install_rejects_invalid_requests_without.note: Refused a snapshot whose membership was not exactly 1, 2, 3; since S4 any non-empty set of nodes 1..=7 is valid, so it now refuses three invalid memberships instead (empty, naming node 0, naming node 8).

file_header_start_fields_validated.note: The invalid vote case voted for node 4; since S4 nodes 1..=7 are valid, so it votes for node 8.

heartbeat_does_not_retire_slow_valid_app.note: A node without a configuration no longer campaigns (S4), so the test starts from a three-node configuration entry at index 1, term 1 instead of an empty log; every term and index it asserts moved up by one, the asserted behaviour is the same.

snapshot_and_wal_consistency_rules.note: Its last row asserted that a snapshot whose term is newer than the WAL's is refused with the files unchanged. The independent review produced exactly that disk state with a real process (a one-message install from a newer term, killed between the snapshot file and the WAL rewrite), after which the node could never start. The row now asserts that the node starts at the snapshot with the snapshot's term and no vote; the other rows are unchanged (lesson 11).

simulation_randomized_invariants.note: The test function was untouched from v1 to S4, but the workload it runs was not: S4 sent every client request to the leader with the highest term, so deposed leaders received no reads and invariant I8 could no longer see a read answered without a confirmation round (the planted mistake passed all 1,000 seeds; under S3's workload it failed at seed 266). The workload now picks any self-believed leader at random and aims extra reads at deposed ones; snapshot chunk sizes vary by seed (7, 13 and 4096 bytes) instead of always 7; a follower's install is interrupted 1 time in 10 instead of 1 in 100. The test additionally asserts that requests reached a deposed leader and that one-message snapshots occurred, so a workload that stops reaching them fails instead of passing (lessons 11 and 12). S5 (14): Also asserts multi_write_batches > 0, so the workload must keep proposing batches of several writes.

real_process_crash_during_snapshot_insta.note: Only its helper calls changed: the snapshot probe takes an optional mode, used by the new real_process_crash_during_install_from_a_newer_term_recovers. Boundaries and assertions are the same.

a_bootstrapped_node_elects_itself_once_i.note: Reads the Delta of each barrier: the vote changes no entry, the no-op is the single entry at index 2. Stronger than the old last_index check.
